# Test Programs

##### Program A
This program stores 10000 in R9 and 1 in R8, then subtracts R8 from R9, storing 
the result in R9. Each of these subtractions is stored as an individual
instruction.

##### Program B
This program performs the same functionality as program A, but does so using a
loop instead of repeated instructions.

##### Program C
This program loads a pseudo-random byte from memory 10000 times in a loop.

##### Program D
This program loads a psuedo-random integer from memory 10000 times in a loop.

##### Program E
This program loads bytes 10000 to 1 sequentially in a loop.

##### Program F
This program performs 10000 jumps, jumping all over the stored program to
psuedo-random locations.
